clinical_safety.purpose: Clinical decision support and retrieval reference; not a substitute for a clinician, local protocols, or emergency services.
clinical_safety.audience_note: Separate lay first aid from clinician-only interventions. Medication lists are not patient-specific prescriptions.
medication_guardrails: Confirm patient identity, age, weight when relevant, allergies, pregnancy status, renal/hepatic function, current medicines, contraindications, and local formulary.
Use current institutional protocols and product labels for exact dosing, preparation, route, monitoring, and contraindications.
Do not delay emergency transport, imaging, reperfusion, CPR, or specialist review to search this knowledge base.
Do not give oral food, drink, or medicines to a person with possible stroke until swallowing safety is assessed.
Medication use in children, pregnancy, older adults, renal impairment, and critical illness requires extra caution and clinician oversight.
clinical_safety.review_status: Draft reference compiled from the sources listed in each file. Must be reviewed and signed off by the institution's clinical lead before clinical deployment.
clinical_safety.jurisdiction_note: Designed as a general reference with India-relevant emergency number context; confirm local emergency numbers, referral pathways, drug availability, and national guidelines.

display_name: Childbirth, labour, postpartum care and advanced maternal age
scope: Pregnancy at age 35 years and older

urgent_maternal_red_flags: Heavy vaginal bleeding, collapse or faintness
Seizure, severe headache, visual changes or upper abdominal pain
Breathing difficulty, chest pain, fever with severe illness
Reduced or absent fetal movement, cord visible/felt, or abnormal fetal heart rate
Waters break with concerning fluid, preterm labour symptoms, or severe hypertension
urgent_newborn_red_flags: Difficulty breathing, blue colour, poor feeding, unusual floppiness or difficult to wake
Fever or low temperature, convulsions, jaundice in first 24 hours
Any newborn deterioration warrants urgent clinical review

items: Confirm gestational age and obstetric history; review comorbidities and medicines.
Monitor blood pressure and symptoms of pre-eclampsia; assess fetal growth/movement and indicated antenatal screening.
For older maternal age, discuss age-related risks without assuming a complication; offer screening/diagnostic options and individualized birth planning.
Maternal vital signs, contractions, bleeding, membrane status and fetal movement
Fetal heart rate assessment and labour progress/cervical examination when appropriate and consented
Assess for infection, hypertensive disease, haemorrhage, malpresentation and cord prolapse
Assess bleeding, uterine tone, pulse, blood pressure, pain, temperature, urination, mental health and feeding
Evaluate heavy bleeding urgently; identify tone, trauma, tissue and thrombin/coagulation causes
Provide follow-up and explicit return precautions for maternal and newborn danger signs

details: First stage: cervical dilation and labour progress; active-phase definitions vary by guideline.
Second stage: full dilation to birth; monitor maternal condition and fetal heart rate.
Third stage: delivery of placenta; active management with a uterotonic is commonly used to reduce postpartum bleeding.
Immediate post-birth observation includes bleeding, uterine tone, vital signs, newborn breathing/temperature and early skin-to-skin/breastfeeding where safe.
Suspect with hypertension after 20 weeks plus proteinuria or maternal organ dysfunction; symptoms can include severe headache, visual symptoms or epigastric/right-upper-quadrant pain.

Severe hypertension or seizure is an obstetric emergency; urgent senior obstetric review, maternal stabilization, magnesium sulfate for seizure prevention/treatment when indicated, and protocol-directed antihypertensive therapy.
Call obstetric emergency team; assess ABCs, quantify blood loss, obtain IV access and labs, warm patient and monitor closely.
Treat likely causes simultaneously: uterine massage and uterotonics for atony, evaluate trauma/retained tissue/coagulopathy, resuscitate and escalate to procedures/surgery when required.
WHO guidance supports early tranexamic acid within 3 hours of birth for diagnosed PPH alongside standard care; exact protocol and contraindications must be checked locally.
Age 35 years or older is a risk marker, not a diagnosis. Individualize counselling and screening.
Review hypertension, diabetes, medication safety, genetic screening choices, fetal growth and timing/place of birth with the obstetric team.
Do not automatically start aspirin or induce labour solely from age without assessing the complete clinical picture and local guideline.

medicines.role: Uterotonic used for prevention and treatment of postpartum haemorrhage and in selected labour protocols.
medicines.safety: Requires correct indication, route, storage, monitoring and institutional protocol; dosing differs by prevention versus treatment.

medicines.role: Adjunct for treatment of diagnosed postpartum haemorrhage; benefit is time-sensitive and WHO recommends administration as soon as possible within 3 hours of birth when indicated.
medicines.safety: Not a replacement for uterotonics, resuscitation or source control; assess contraindications and use the local PPH bundle.

medicines.role: Prevention/treatment of eclamptic seizures in appropriate severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia pathways.
medicines.safety: Monitor respiratory status, reflexes, urine output and toxicity; calcium gluconate may be used as antidote under protocol.

medicines.role: Agents used by clinicians to treat severe hypertension in pregnancy/postpartum, depending on patient and protocol.
medicines.safety: Urgent monitoring and obstetric oversight required; do not self-medicate.

medicines.role: May be used when preterm birth is likely within the guideline-defined gestational window to improve neonatal outcomes.
medicines.safety: Eligibility depends on gestational age, likelihood of birth and maternal/fetal context.

current_medicine_landscape.note: These are established guideline-supported obstetric medicines, not a market trend ranking.
key_groups: Oxytocin and other protocol-selected uterotonics for PPH prevention/treatment
Tranexamic acid as early adjunct in diagnosed PPH
Magnesium sulfate for severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia when indicated
Protocol-selected antihypertensives for severe pregnancy/postpartum hypertension
Antenatal corticosteroids for eligible threatened preterm birth
